e.etymology: From Hebrew Asayah, the Lord has made. Several minor Old Testament figures bear the name, including a servant of King Josiah. Parents today often choose it as a cousin of Isaiah and Asa.

e.meaning: church, from the Scottish town of Paisley
e.etymology: A respelling of Paisley, a Scottish surname from the town near Glasgow, whose name probably goes back to Latin basilica, church. The town's weavers gave their name to the paisley teardrop pattern.

assoc.t: paisley, the swirling teardrop fabric pattern

e.meaning: carter, one who hauls goods by cart
e.etymology: A K spelling of Cartier, a French surname for a carter. As a first name it is American and recent, and borrows the glamour of the Paris jeweler Cartier.

assoc.t: Cartier, the French luxury jeweler and watchmaker

e.etymology: A 20th-century name of unclear origin, perhaps from a rare Irish surname or from Darragh, oak. Darrin Stephens, the husband on the 1960s sitcom Bewitched, helped spread it.

e.meaning: claw of a bird of prey
e.etymology: The English word for a raptor's claw, from Old French talon, heel. Talon is also an old surname, but the modern first name is taken from the word.

assoc.t: talon, the claw of an eagle or hawk

e.etymology: A variant of Hadley, an English surname from place names meaning heather clearing, from Old English haeth and leah. Hadleigh is the spelling of towns in Suffolk and Essex.
From Arabic layan, softness or gentleness, and also taken to mean a life of ease. It has been among the most popular girls' names in the Arab world in recent years.
From the Irish surnames O Braonain, descendant of Braonan, from braon, drop or moisture, and O Branain, from bran, raven. It is also used as a variant of Brendan.
namesakes: Brennan Huff (Will Ferrell's character in Step Brothers)

e.meaning: joy, gladness, by way of Letitia
e.etymology: A pet form of Letitia, from Latin laetitia, joy, and of its medieval English form Lettice. Lettie was common as a given name in the late 1800s.
A spelling of Jayla, a 20th-century American coinage that joins Jay to the -la ending of Kayla and Layla.

assoc.t: Jaylah, the alien ally in Star Trek Beyond

e.etymology: A spelling of Shepherd, the English occupational surname, from Old English words for sheep and herder. This is the spelling of astronaut Alan Shepard's surname.
namesakes: Shepard Fairey (street artist behind the Obama Hope poster)
Commander Shepard (hero of the Mass Effect video games)

assoc.t: Commander Shepard, hero of the Mass Effect games

e.etymology: A German pet form of Rosemarie, made famous by the actress Romy Schneider, and a short form of Romina and Romana. The Hebrew name Romi, from rom, height, is spelled Romy too.
namesakes: Romy White (Mira Sorvino in Romy and Michele's High School Reunion)

assoc.t: Romy of Romy and Michele's High School Reunion

e.etymology: From Turkish eren, a holy or enlightened person. Its recent rise in the US follows Eren Yeager, the hero of the Japanese manga and anime Attack on Titan.

assoc.t: Eren Yeager, hero of the anime Attack on Titan

e.note: Spoken aloud it is easily heard as Erin or Aaron.

e.etymology: An English surname for someone who lived by a pear tree, from Old English pyrige. It has also been a pet form of Peregrine.
namesakes: Perry the Platypus (secret-agent pet in Phineas and Ferb)

assoc.t: Perry the Platypus of Phineas and Ferb
Perry Mason, the TV defense attorney

e.meaning: giant; one of the elder gods of Greek myth
e.etymology: From the Titans of Greek myth, the generation of gods who ruled before Zeus and the Olympians. In English a titan is a person of great size, strength or importance.

assoc.t: the Titans of Greek myth; a titan of industry
Tennessee Titans, the NFL team
Titan, the largest moon of Saturn
Titan, the OceanGate submersible that imploded in 2023

e.etymology: An English surname from a place in Yorkshire, built on an Old English personal name, Tynni. As a girls' name it follows socialite Tinsley Mortimer, who became known in the 2000s.
namesakes: Tinsley Mortimer (socialite on The Real Housewives of New York City)

assoc.t: Tinsley Mortimer, socialite and reality TV star

e.etymology: An older spelling of Spanish Mateo and Italian Matteo, revived alongside the fashionable French Matheo. All are forms of Matthew, from Hebrew Mattityahu, gift of Yahweh.
A spelling of Maisie, a Scottish pet form of Mairead, the Gaelic Margaret, from the Greek word for pearl. The z spelling was the common American one around 1900.
A modern American blend of Ava and Lynn; it can also be read as a spelling of the medieval name Aveline.
A spelling of Zuri, from the Swahili word for beautiful or good. This spelling is the one LeBron James chose for his daughter, Zhuri, born in 2014.

From the Hill of Tara, seat of Ireland's high kings; the name spread after Tara, the plantation in Gone with the Wind. A separate Tara, from Sanskrit for star, is a goddess in Hindu and Buddhist tradition.

assoc.t: Tara, the plantation in Gone with the Wind
Hill of Tara, seat of Ireland's high kings
Tara, a goddess in Buddhism and Hinduism

e.etymology: The Spanish spelling of Kenya, used as a girls' name in Latin America and by Latino families in the US. The country takes its name from Mount Kenya.
A modern spelling in the family of Aleah, Alaia and Aaliyah, with no single established source.
An American spelling of Giovanna, the Italian feminine of Giovanni (John), from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious. The spelling follows Gia and Gianna.

e.meaning: father of peace, by way of Axel
e.etymology: The spelling coined by Guns N' Roses singer Axl Rose. Axel is the Scandinavian form of the Biblical Absalom, Hebrew for father of peace.
namesakes: Axl Rose (lead singer of Guns N' Roses)
Axl Heck (the eldest son on the sitcom The Middle)

assoc.t: Axl Rose, Guns N' Roses frontman

e.note: Sounds exactly like axle, the car part.

e.etymology: An English occupational surname, a shortened form of Forster, forester. It can also come from the word foster, as in a foster parent or child.

assoc.t: foster care; to foster, meaning to nurture
Foster's, the Australian lager

e.etymology: From the English word and the surname Stone, given to someone who lived near a notable stone or worked with stone, from Old English stan.

assoc.t: stone, the everyday word for rock

e.etymology: An English spelling of Irish Ciara, the feminine of Ciaran, from ciar, dark or black. Saint Ciara was a 7th-century Irish abbess.
The Spanish form of Jairus, from Hebrew Yair, he enlightens. In the Gospels Jairus is the synagogue leader whose young daughter Jesus raises from death.
A spelling of Scarlett, an English surname for a seller of scarlet, a fine cloth, from Old French escarlate. Scarlett O'Hara of Gone with the Wind turned the surname into a girls' name.
A modern American name in the mold of Isaiah and Azariah, combining their sounds. It has no separate meaning of its own.
The Amharic and Tigrinya form of Jeremiah, from Hebrew Yirmeyahu. It is used in Ethiopian and Eritrean families and became known in the US as the given name of rapper Nipsey Hussle.
namesakes: Nipsey Hussle (rapper whose given name was Ermias)

assoc.t: Ermias, given name of rapper Nipsey Hussle
